input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Wolfspeed

ownership.as_of: 2025-09-29 (change of control); share count as of 2026-10-30
ownership.value: Public company, NYSE: WOLF. Change of control via Chapter 11: emerged 2025-09-29; old common stock (156,479,390 shares) cancelled; pre-petition creditors received ~95% of ~25,840,656 new common shares, old equity ~5% (3% initial + final 2% released after CFIUS clearance 2026-01-30); Renesas Electronics America received 16,852,372 new shares plus warrants for 4,943,555 shares at $23.95 and a board seat with 9.9% voting / 39.9% ownership caps; re-domesticated from North Carolina to Delaware; no 10%+ beneficial holders as of 2025-09-19; 53,581,878 shares outstanding as of 2026-10-30.

debt_events.summary: Wolfspeed, Inc. and Wolfspeed Texas LLC filed voluntary prepackaged Chapter 11 petitions in U.S. Bankruptcy Court, Southern District of Texas, Houston Division; filing constituted an event of default under the 1.75% (2026), 0.25% (2028) and 1.875% (2029) convertible notes, the Renesas Customer Refundable Deposit Agreement and the Senior Secured Notes indenture, making obligations immediately due and payable (stayed). Total funded debt was ~$6.7 billion per the disclosure statement.

Restructuring Support Agreement with holders of >97% of Senior Secured Notes due 2030, Renesas Electronics America, and holders of >67% of convertible notes: debt to be cut ~70% (~$4.6 billion) and annual cash interest ~60%; convertible noteholders to receive $296M New 2L Takeback Notes and 56.3% of new common stock; Renesas to receive $204M New 2L Convertible Notes and 38.7% of new common stock plus 5% warrants; existing equity to receive 3.0%-5.0% of new common stock; fully backstopped $301.13M rights offering of New 2L Convertible Notes at 91.3242% of principal.
Bankruptcy court confirmed the prepackaged Plan of Reorganization; emergence expected within weeks with ~70% debt reduction.

Emerged from Chapter 11 (Plan Effective Date; fresh-start accounting): issued $1,259,210,128 New Senior Secured Notes due 2030 (secured by substantially all assets) and redeemed $277.5M of Existing Senior Secured Notes at 109.875%; issued ~$180.7M plus $120.45M backstop-purchased New 2.5% Convertible Second-Lien Notes due 2031 (plus $30.25M backstop premium notes), ~$296.4M New 7.00%/12.00% Second-Lien PIK Toggle Notes due 2031, and ~$203.6M New Renesas 2L Convertible Notes; terminated the 2026/2028/2029 convertible indentures, the Existing Senior Secured Notes indenture and the Renesas CRD Agreement. Per the pro forma 8-K exhibit, liabilities subject to compromise of $7,315.3M were eliminated and pro forma total debt at emergence was ~$2,151.1M fair value.

CFIUS formally cleared the issuance of equity to Renesas, completing a key component of the court-approved restructuring; escrowed shares (16,852,372 to Renesas and final 871,287 shares to legacy equity) cleared for release; Renesas received a board seat.

Refinanced ~$476 million of first-lien debt (new financing: $379.0M proceeds from 1.5L Convertible Notes and $96.9M from New Common Stock and Pre-Funded Warrants), reducing the total debt balance by $97 million and annual interest expense by an estimated $62 million; payments on long-term borrowings of $716.4 million in the Successor period through 2026-03-29.
Subsequent event disclosed in the 10-Q: Wolfspeed entered a Senior Secured Delayed Draw Term Loan Facility (line of credit) with tranche one and remaining tranches disclosed.

Announced a conditional 30-year, $1.5 billion loan commitment from the U.S. Department of War (Office of Strategic Capital) to advance domestic wide bandgap supply; loan remains conditional (due diligence, definitive agreements, government approvals, conditions to closing) and is expected to deliver significant annual interest savings upon completion.

credit_ratings.summary: CreditRiskMonitor commercial credit report preview records 'Emerged from Bankruptcy on 9/29/2025' for Wolfspeed Inc (Durham, NC); its Moody's/Fitch/DBRS rating fields show '-' (not displayed on the public preview), so no current agency rating could be verified from an opened page.

DebtCanary (private-credit-risk monitor) scores Wolfspeed 8/10 (high risk, sector average 2.5/10), citing the Chapter 11 filing of 2025-07-01, $1.7B long-term debt, negative interest coverage (-31.2x: operating loss -$1.3B vs $43M interest expense) and a ~7-month cash runway on operating burn; it states WOLF 'shows elevated refinancing risk that warrants close monitoring'. This is a model score, not an S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating.

missing_fields: Current S&P, Moody's and Fitch credit ratings and outlooks, and any rating action in the last 12 months - no rating-agency page for Wolfspeed was obtainable; CreditRiskMonitor's Moody's/Fitch/DBRS fields are not displayed on its public preview
Tax liens, judgments against Wolfspeed as defendant, or collection suits by suppliers - none found on opened pages (CreditRiskMonitor shows the report sections exist but contents are paywalled)
output.risk_rationale: Wolfspeed is 13 months out of a prepackaged Chapter 11 (filed 2025-06-30, emerged 2025-09-29) in which $7,315.3 million of liabilities subject to compromise were eliminated and legacy convertible/CRD debt was extinguished — unsecured creditors converted to deeply discounted securities and old equity kept only ~5%, confirming severe credit impairment in the recent past. It is not yet a self-sustaining credit: Q1 FY2027 (quarter ended 2026-09-27) revenue fell to $155.0 million from $196.8 million a year earlier with a (22)% GAAP gross margin, $(112.8) million operating loss, $(54.7) million adjusted EBITDA and $(84.2) million operating cash flow, and cash plus short-term investments declined to $995.1 million (from $1,088.6 million at 2026-06-28) with no committed revolver — only a conditional $1.5 billion U.S. Department of War OSC loan commitment and a new delayed-draw term loan (2026-10-07) not yet funded. At the current ~$90-100 million quarterly cash burn, liquidity covers roughly 2-2.5 years absent improvement, and the still-uncleared conditional OSC loan plus additional-headcount-reduction and facility-closure costs (2025/2026 restructuring plans) argue for treating counterparty exposure as high risk despite the post-emergence deleveraging to ~$1.68 billion of funded debt.

distress_signals.summary: Wolfspeed raised going-concern doubts (going-concern language included in the 10-Q footnotes for the quarter ended 2025-03-30), citing changing U.S. trade policies and weakening EV demand; shares sank on the news and it disclosed it may pursue a balance-sheet fix 'through an in-court solution'.

FY2025 10-K/earnings release: goodwill fully impaired ($359.2M charge), restructuring and other expenses of $417.6M, cash and short-term investments fell from $2,174.6M to $955.4M during FY2025, negative shareholders' equity of $(447.1)M, and forward-looking statements reference 'substantial doubt about Wolfspeed's ability to continue as a going concern' and possible NYSE delisting during Chapter 11.

Announced reduction of ~180 employees at Durham and Siler City materials operations, after laying off 20% of its global workforce and closing several facilities in 2024 (~$200M savings); stock hit a 27-year low in March 2025 amid uncertainty over the $750M CHIPS Act grant.

CFO Neill Reynolds announced departure as EVP & CFO effective 2025-05-30 while the company was in active lender negotiations; interim CFO Kevin Speirits took over; permanent CFO Gregor van Issum appointed effective 2025-09-01. CEO Robert Feurle appointed May 2025; new COO role created.

Entire pre-bankruptcy board (Tom Werner, Glenda Dorchak, John Hodge, Darren Jackson, Duy-Loan Le, Marvin Riley) departed at emergence; new directors appointed (Chairman Anthony M. Abate, Michael Bokan, Hong Q. Hou, Eric Musser).

Ongoing restructuring: additional headcount reductions implemented in Q2 and Q4 fiscal 2026 with further severance costs in Q1 fiscal 2027 ($14.3M restructuring and other expenses), $4.0M idle-facility costs from a recent facility closure, and an $11.8M supply-contract renegotiation penalty; risk factors cite ongoing impacts of the 2025 Chapter 11 reorganization, the need for additional funding, customer concentration and take-or-pay supplier commitments. Revenue declined to $155.0M from $196.8M year over year with a (22)% GAAP gross margin.

payment_behaviour.summary: On the Chapter 11 filing Wolfspeed stated it was operating as usual and paying vendors in the ordinary course; first-day court relief anticipated vendors and other unsecured creditors being paid in full in the ordinary course of business (all non-creditor-plan unsecured creditors ultimately unimpaired under the plan).

Wolfspeed as plaintiff sued Navitas Semiconductor Corp. and GeneSiC Semiconductor LLC in U.S. District Court (M.D.N.C., Case 1:24-cv-01038) seeking not less than $1,688,625 plus 1.5%/month interest for 1,975 delivered but unpurchased wafer units — a collection dispute evidencing customer payment/receivable exposure on its order book (the customer's $4.27M 5,000-unit order).

Wolfspeed sued bulk-gas supplier Air Products & Chemicals in North Carolina federal court, alleging the supplier reneged on an equipment-removal obligation under their contract and that Wolfspeed suspended service fees — a live supplier dispute in the wake of its restructuring (Law360).
